# Modding Horizon

> Horizon is Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 in Rust. A mod is one `.hmod`: content (`assets/`, `data/`) and, for a code mod, a Rust crate built natively by the launcher or to `mod.wasm`, against the `mod_api` crate (`horizon-mod-api`).

Rules for code: implement `mod_api::Hooks` at the crate root with `#[mod_api::horizon_mod]`; prefer a hook or Part method; change the game's own code only through the native route (`[[native.mixin]]`, `[[native.loop]]`, `[[native.bridge]]`, `[[native.module]]`, native only). Hook names follow NeoForge 26.3; events are `&mut`; writes take a `ServerHost`. The id and version come only from `horizon-mod.toml`; ids are `[a-z0-9_]`. A mod is `[native]` or `[wasm]`, never both; unknown manifest fields are refused.

## Getting started

- [Installing and using mods](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/blob/main/docs/modding/src/start/installing.md)
- [Your first content mod](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/blob/main/docs/modding/src/start/first-content-mod.md)
- [Your first native mod](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/blob/main/docs/modding/src/start/first-mod.md)
- [Your first WebAssembly mod](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/blob/main/docs/modding/src/start/first-wasm-mod.md)
- [Writing hooks](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/blob/main/docs/modding/src/start/writing-hooks.md): the crate root, events, hosts and listener order.
